repository.implementation_state: separate firewall-hardening change after the immutable baseline

scope.objective: persist the accepted Splunk-source restriction for Docker-published TCP 8091 across an ir-core reboot

firewall.ufw: active with default incoming and routed deny; not effective as the Docker published-port authority

service_ordering.docker: enabled; after network-online.target, containerd.service, docker.socket, and firewalld.service

design.mechanism: idempotent Alert2IR rule reconciler invoked by Docker systemd ExecStartPre and verified by ExecStartPost
design.fail_safe: ExecStartPre creates/reconciles DOCKER-USER before dockerd restores published containers; any apply failure prevents Docker startup. ExecStartPost verifies the backend and first FORWARD jump.
design.narrow_ownership: only the two comment-owned rules and their exact accepted un-commented legacy equivalents are reconciled; the chain and unrelated rules are never flushed

rejected_alternatives.iptables_persistent_or_netfilter_persist: not installed and a full static restore would own unrelated dynamic Docker and host policy
rejected_alternatives.native_nftables_configuration: Docker is using the iptables backend and its Docker 29 native nftables backend is not enabled
rejected_alternatives.ufw_rule: Docker-published traffic reaches Docker forwarding rules before ordinary UFW input policy
rejected_alternatives.firewalld: not installed and adding another firewall manager is unnecessary
rejected_alternatives.post_docker_only_oneshot: would leave a possible interval in which restored published containers precede source filtering
